newsitem.title: USA: U.S. proposes to stay out of "brownfields" cleanup.
newsitem.headline: U.S. proposes to stay out of "brownfields" cleanup.

text.p: In a move to spur land redevelopment, the federal government Thursday proposed to stay out of cleaning up abandoned industrial sites or seeking to recover cleanup costs, and let states guide those projects.

The proposal was designed to reassure financial and real estate investors who are reluctant to revive lightly polluted properties, called "brownfields", because they fear the U.S. government might later make them pay cleanup costs for past contamination under the Superfund toxic waste law.

"The guidance removes a perceived obstacle to redeveloping property with low levels of contamination that can contribute to the economies of our nation's cities," Assistant Attorney General Lois Schiffer said in a statement.
Under the draft guidance, the U.S. government will not step in to assess brownfield sites as long as they are cleaned up under state voluntary programs that meet minimum federal standards.
The proposal also aims to help property owners and states find out how much contamination there is at the sites and whether it threatens human health or the environment.
EPA estimates there are 450,000 brownfield sites in blighted areas across the country.
